en-US.description:
Create timed SRT subtitles from video and audio on your Mac. Transcribe locally, then optionally translate subtitles using your ChatGPT plan.

TRANSCRIBE ON YOUR MAC
Use the included whisper.cpp engine with Metal acceleration. Detect the spoken language automatically or choose it yourself. Long recordings are split into audio chunks, with subtitle timing restored to the original recording. Transcription does not require a ChatGPT account.

TRANSLATE WITH CHATGPT
Choose Continue with ChatGPT and authorize plan usage. The app retrieves the models available to your account and lets you choose a model. Automatic selection follows the first model in the server's list; it does not guarantee the newest release or best translation quality. Only subtitle text and translation instructions are sent for translation. Audio and video are processed locally.

KEEP CONTROL OF YOUR FILES
Reuse matching SRT files or extract supported text subtitle tracks. Work through a file queue, view progress, and cancel processing. The app checks subtitle numbering, cue counts and timestamps before accepting translations. Save SRT files or embed subtitles in supported video containers. Failed translations preserve source subtitles. An embedded video replaces the original only after output validation.

SETUP AND REQUIREMENTS
Requires macOS 14 or later and an Apple Silicon Mac. The current interface is in Korean. FFmpeg, FFprobe and Whisper are included. Download a speech model before transcription; Large v3 Turbo is approximately 1.6 GB. Authorize the input folders where subtitles will be saved.

FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
The app is free and its own source code is available under the MIT license. Third-party tools retain their respective licenses. ChatGPT translation requires an eligible account and your approval, uses your ChatGPT plan or credits, and is subject to OpenAI availability and usage limits. The app does not include a ChatGPT subscription. Model downloads and translation require an internet connection. No separate Codex installation or API key is needed for this version.

Supported inputs include MP4, MOV, MKV, M4V, AVI, WebM, FLV, M4A, WAV and MP3. Output is SRT; subtitle embedding depends on the video container. Image-based subtitle tracks are not extracted as text.

review.notes:
SubGen is a free native macOS subtitle utility for Apple Silicon (macOS 14+). The interface follows the system language: English, Korean, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian (other languages show English). It has no app account, subscription, in-app purchase, API-key setup or external CLI requirement. Local transcription and subtitle embedding work without signing in.

LOCAL WORKFLOW
1. Click Prepare Job in the upper right. FFmpeg, FFprobe and whisper.cpp are included. Choose a speech model and download it. Tiny is about 78 MB and is suitable for a quick test; larger models improve accuracy. Model data is downloaded from Hugging Face into the app container.
2. Click Choose Files…, or drop an audio/video file onto the main window.
3. Expand Work Settings. Choose the source language (Auto-Detect is available) and the output, and leave translation languages unchecked.
4. Click Create Subtitles. When prompted, click Allow Folder Access for the input folder so generated subtitles can be written beside the media. A matching existing SRT may be reused.
5. The Embed Subtitles in Video output embeds subtitles in supported video containers. The original video is replaced only after validation; failed translations preserve source subtitles.
SubGen is a single-window app: closing the main window quits the app (the queue is saved).

OPTIONAL TRANSLATION (no account needed)
On macOS 26 or later, expand Work Settings, set Translation Method to Apple Translation (On-Device), set the source language (for example English), check a target language such as Korean, then click Create Subtitles. If macOS asks to download translation languages, approve it. Translation runs on the Mac with Apple's Translation framework; subtitles are not sent to the developer or any translation service.

Alternatively choose ChatGPT and click Continue with ChatGPT. This opens OpenAI authorization and asks for consent to use an eligible ChatGPT account's plan/credits. Only subtitle text and translation instructions are sent to OpenAI. This option is subject to OpenAI account eligibility, availability and usage limits.

ENTITLEMENTS
com.apple.security.network.server is used only by the optional Sign in with ChatGPT translation. OpenAI's sign-in for native apps redirects the OAuth authorization code to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth/callback (RFC 8252 loopback redirect). When the user clicks Continue with ChatGPT, SubGen opens a single-use listener bound only to the IPv4 loopback interface on an ephemeral port, accepts one callback and closes it. The app never listens otherwise and accepts no connections from other hosts. com.apple.security.network.client downloads speech models from Hugging Face and sends ChatGPT translation requests.
